scope: identity-model fix in tools/strategy_farm/compile_work_items.py classify_candidate (STALE_INCLUDE_CLOSURE class) plus one governed rebuild for QM5_41347/NDX.DWX; no strategy, backtest-verdict, pipeline-gate, live, or portfolio-gate authority is claimed or exercised

root_cause.summary: classify_candidate's USABLE_CURRENT_COMPILE_VERDICT_EXISTS check tracked only (mq5_sha256, ex5_sha256). It had no visibility into framework/include/QM/QM_MagicResolver.mqh (auto-generated by framework/scripts/update_magic_resolver.py from framework/registry/magic_numbers.csv), whose magic-lookup arrays are statically compiled into the .ex5. Adding a second magic-registry row for QM5_41347 (NDX.DWX/413470001, 2026-09-19) did not change the .mq5 or invalidate the 2026-09-05 .ex5's own hash, so the identity model kept reporting the stale binary as 'current' and refused any rebuild.

prior_compile_ok_row.note: both hashes remain unchanged today; this is why the QM5_21505/QM5_13054 stale-binary precedent (no prior COMPILE_OK for the exact hash pair) did not apply here

registry_state_at_2026-09-19-registratio.note: QM_MAGIC_REGISTRY_SHA256 embedded in framework/include/QM/QM_MagicResolver.mqh after the 2026-09-19 CSV edit + resolver regen that added the NDX.DWX/413470001 row; the 2026-09-05 .ex5 predates this value and cannot resolve slot 1

fix.mechanism: STALE_INCLUDE_CLOSURE_REGISTRATIONS (append-only per-EA data registration, parallel in spirit to BACKLOG_SOURCE_REPAIR_REGISTRATIONS) plus a forward-looking self-describing check
functions_added: _current_include_closure_sha256(repo_root) -> str | None: reads QM_MAGIC_REGISTRY_SHA256 out of framework/include/QM/QM_MagicResolver.mqh
_stale_include_closure_authorized(...): binds an authority string to an exact (ea_label, ea_id, source_sha256) triple and pins this evidence file's sha256
_stale_include_closure_artifact_bindings(...): evidence pointer surfaced in classify_candidate's source_repair_artifact_bindings
fix.classify_candidate_change: current_compile_ok now excludes any row (a) whose own recorded payload_json.include_closure_sha256 (stamped at enqueue time going forward) no longer matches the live QM_MAGIC_REGISTRY_SHA256 (auto-detected, no registration needed), or (b) named explicitly in a matching STALE_INCLUDE_CLOSURE_REGISTRATIONS entry's stale_compile_ok_work_item_ids (for rows compiled before include_closure_sha256 was recorded, like 245ee112). Excluded ids are surfaced as stale_include_closure_work_item_ids in the return dict for evidence; they are never silently dropped.
fix.enqueue_change: enqueue_compile_eas and the build-task-triggered enqueue path both now stamp payload_json.include_closure_sha256 = candidate['include_closure_sha256'] at enqueue time, so every future COMPILE_OK row is self-describing and a later registry regen auto-invalidates it without needing a new registration.
fix.blast_radius: narrows current_compile_ok only for rows matching an exact registered (ea_label, ea_id, source_sha256) triple, or rows that themselves recorded a now-stale include_closure_sha256. Every other EA's classify_candidate outcome is unchanged: with no registration and no recorded field (the status quo for all pre-existing rows except this one), stale_include_closure_ids stays empty and current_compile_ok is untouched.

rebuild.note: farmctl enqueue-compile --source-repair-authority <this authority> followed by release_compile_wave.py --apply; classify_candidate now reports eligible=true / source_repair_authorized=true because 245ee112 is excluded from current_compile_ok. Command transcript and resulting COMPILE_OK evidence recorded separately in this same evidence directory (compile_dispatch.json) once the terminal fleet actually executes the compile.

not_performed: no waiver of EX5_ALREADY_PRESENT/WORK_ITEMS_EXIST/BOUND_SETFILE_HASH_EXISTS beyond the standard FORCE_REBUILD_WAIVABLE_REASONS path that already applies once source_repair_authorized is true for any authority
no change to the USABLE_CURRENT_COMPILE_VERDICT_EXISTS guard for any EA other than the one named in this registration or one that itself recorded a stale include_closure_sha256

safety.gate_criteria_unchanged: this is an identity/staleness fix in the compile work-item classifier, not a Q02-Q13 gate threshold or contract-criteria change
